summary: The audit checks the 44 graduate units. Your path depends on where you earned your LLM: with a Stanford LLM or JSM, 35 of its units count (26 or more in Law School courses) and you add three approved courses of 3 or more units in the first JSD year; with an LLM from elsewhere, you complete 44 residency units here, at most 9 outside the Law School. You move these courses in by hand. Checked by hand: three quarters in residence, 9-12 approved first-year units including a methodology course, the first-year oral exam, the reading committee form, the dissertation and its defense, the JSD colloquium every year in residence, and the graduation application. No courses at other law schools count.

ofqDwlr6-text.why: "All JSD candidates must pass an oral examination at the end of the first academic year of the JSD program ... and must successfully defend their dissertation orally at the completion of the program." The first-year oral exam is rule ov-first-oral and the defense is rule ov-defense; the rest describes how they run.

iwHWtFFx-text.why: "At least one of these three courses must provide either advanced methodological training and the remaining courses must provide further study in a substantive field related to the student’s doctoral research and all three must be approved by the student’s dissertation chair or by the Associate Dean for Graduate Studies." The same three approved courses as rules ov-first-year and ov-methods, which are checked by hand; directed research counts only by petition, which is part of that approval.

freeform-text.why: The page's requirements text lists the same requirements the rules here carry: "Three quarters in residency during the first JSD year" (ov-residency), "9 - 12 approved quarter units during the first JSD year, including at least one methodological course" (ov-methods), the first-year oral exam (ov-first-oral), the reading committee form (ov-committee), the dissertation and defense (ov-dissertation, ov-defense), the colloquium (Fj4EHwdh), the graduation application (ov-graduation), and "Credits earned to meet the JSM requirements will count toward 35 of these quarter units. At least 26 of those 35 units must be in Law School courses" (ov-llm-credit). "No student may take more than eight units in a single quarter" is an enrollment limit, not something to complete.

fsmOmz4N.why: "Credits earned to meet the Stanford-based LLM or JSM (SPILS) requirements will count toward 35 of the 44 units" with "At least 26 of those 35 units must be in Law School courses", and "First-Year Enrollment: 3 courses of at least 3 units each, for a minimum of 9 but no more than 15 units." The units are spread over another degree's record (the Stanford LLM or JSM) or limited by where they were taken, so the student moves the courses in.
